sam: Planned AZ drain + model-failover rehearsal Fri 2026-04-24 03:00-04:30 UTC. Purpose: validate graceful placement and automatic fallback to quantized model-variants during node drains. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/az-drain-model-failover (internal). Please ack if you own high-priority routes that must be pinned. :loud_sound:
ellie: Ack. Which GPU pools/variants are in scope?
sam: Scope: gpu-pool-x, model family: redwood-open-7b -> fallback redwood-open-7b-q4 for best-effort traffic. High-priority tenants stay on full model. Canary: internal-dev, beta, control-prod-3pct.
ops-eng: We'll simulate a 20% node drain in az-b for 10m, then restore. Traffic shift 10% -> 40% over 15m.
sre_oncall: Status page blurb draft: "Planned AZ drain may increase latency for best-effort routes; high-priority tenants will be preserved. No data loss expected."
ci-bot: Pre-checks: smoke-tests OK, canary dashboards green, jobs queued: drain-sim-2598765432.
ellie: Rollback criteria?
sam: Abort if 5xx > 1% sustained for 10m OR model-fallback error rate > 0.5% for 10m. Success criteria: quantized fallback serving <= +150ms p99 overhead and no client errors.
ops-eng: We'll enable quiet-window 02:45-04:45 UTC and pause noncritical batch jobs. Excluding partner-org: add sticky pin label partner:high.
sre_oncall: I'll set up dedicated channel #az-drain-2598765432 and update rota/escalation.
ellie: Can we warm kvcache prefixes before failing over to reduce tail latency?
sam: Yes, pre-warm step is in runbook. Sequence: 1) pre-warm KV prefixes 30m prior, 2) enable canary shift, 3) drain nodes, 4) monitor metrics, 5) ramp back.
ops-eng: Noted. Deploy-bot: scheduled job drain-sim-2598765432 at 03:00 UTC.
sam: I'll post live updates in this thread during the window. Final reminder Thu 16:00 PT. Flag exclusions here before Thu EOD. :eyes:
